sentences.text: Sacisaurus was a silesaurid dinosauriform living in the Late Triassic Caturrita Formation of southern Brazil.
Based on the largest femur, this animal measured approximately 1.1 meters in length and stood 35 centimeters high.
Its long, strong legs suggest it was a fast animal.
The largest teeth of Sacisaurus were only 3 millimeters long.
Fossil collectors found 35 right femurs but only one left femur of Sacisaurus.
Sacisaurus possessed a bone at the tip of its jaw that resembles the ornithischian predentary bone.
Scientists discovered Sacisaurus in 2001 in Agudo, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
The official announcement of Sacisaurus was made on November 1, 2006, at the University of São Paulo in Ribeirão Preto.
The scientific description of Sacisaurus was published in Historical Biology on October 30, 2006.
Research at the University of São Paulo revealed that Sacisaurus was not a dinosaur but a reptile from a different lineage still linked to dinosaur ancestors.
The parent group of Sacisaurus is Sulcimentisauria.
Sacisaurus belongs to the family Silesauridae.
The Paleobi Database classifies Sacisaurus under the class Ornithischia.
Sacisaurus lived in southern Brazil approximately 220 million years ago during the Triassic period.
Sacisaurus lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
PhD student Jonathan Bittencourt presented conclusions leading to the reclassification of Sacisaurus at the 7th Brazilian Symposium of Vertebrate Paleontology.
Bittencourt's thesis found that the jaw and teeth of Sacisaurus evolved independently of ornithischians.
